question: If I’m tracking a federal regulatory proposal, what’s the difference between looking in Part I and Part II of the Canada Gazette?
generated_answer:
The Canada Gazette is divided into three parts: Part I, Part II, and Part III. Part I contains official government notices, orders, and proclamations. Part II contains proposed regulations, which are open for public comment. Part III contains final regulations, as well as other information such as appointment notices and certain types of legal notices. If you’re tracking a federal regulatory proposal, you would look in Part II of the Canada Gazette, as this is where proposed regulations are published for public comment. Once a regulation is finalized, it would be published in Part III of the Canada Gazette. 

For more information, you can refer to the Government of Canada's Canada Gazette website: https://www.gazette.gc.ca/ 

Please note that the Canada Gazette is not the only source for tracking regulatory proposals. You may also want to check the Government of Canada's Regulatory Registry (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/gov/regulatory-registry.html) and the department or agency responsible for the proposal for more information. 

If you have any further questions or need more specific information, feel free to ask!
